name: Harambe
blurb: The Cincinnati Zoo gorilla killed in May 2016, who became 2016's biggest meme
title: Harambe Meme: Who Harambe Was and Why It Became a Meme
description: Harambe was a gorilla shot at the Cincinnati Zoo on 28 May 2016 after a three-year-old boy fell into his enclosure. Tributes and jokes made him 2016's top meme.
h1: Who was Harambe, and why is he a meme?
answer: Harambe was a 17-year-old western lowland gorilla, a critically endangered species, who lived at the Cincinnati Zoo in Ohio. On 28 May 2016 a three-year-old boy climbed into his enclosure, and zoo staff shot Harambe to protect the child, which set off an international debate. Over summer 2016 sincere tributes and absurdist jokes about him spread so widely that Vox called Harambe the meme of the year, and "RIP Harambe" is still used today.

body: Harambe was born on 27 May 1999 at the Gladys Porter Zoo in Brownsville, Texas, and moved to the Cincinnati Zoo and Botanical Garden in September 2014. On 28 May 2016, one day after his 17th birthday, a three-year-old boy got through a barrier and fell into the gorilla habitat. Harambe carried and dragged the boy through the water moat, and the zoo's emergency response team shot him. Defenders of the decision, such as the longtime zoo director and TV host Jack Hanna, pointed out that a tranquilliser dart could take minutes to work. The boy's injuries were not life-threatening.

The decision was debated around the world: whether the zoo had another option, how the barrier was built, and who was responsible. Prosecutors announced in June 2016 that the boy's mother would not face charges.

head: Date
Event
rows: Harambe is killed on 28 May; news and video of the incident spread worldwide.
Tributes, Photoshops and joke catchphrases about Harambe flood social media through the summer.
The Cincinnati Zoo asks the public to stop the memes; later that month it deletes its Twitter account after constant trolling, returning about two months later.
Vox names Harambe the meme of the year.
A bronze Harambe statue is placed in Bowling Green Park in New York City.
A documentary, Harambe, is released on World Gorilla Day.

body: The meme mixes real grief with absurd, sometimes edgy humour, which is why the zoo found it painful. Common forms:

ul: "RIP Harambe" and "Never forget Harambe" as a nostalgic, semi-ironic tribute.
Jokes that Harambe's death was the moment the timeline "went wrong", blaming later bad news on it.
Edits that add Harambe to famous photos, songs and video games.

body: Harambe is a classic 2016 meme that comes back every anniversary. The incident also had lasting effects: it renewed public discussion about zoo safety and about western lowland gorillas, which are critically endangered in the wild. The Cincinnati Zoo introduced a new gorilla, Mshindi, in 2017.

body.note: Harambe was a real animal. The zoo's director said staff were "not amused" by the memes and that they made moving on harder. Most people now mention him with affection, but jokes about his death can still come across as hurtful.

faq.a: A three-year-old boy fell into his enclosure on 28 May 2016 and Harambe dragged him through the moat. The zoo judged the child to be in danger, and a tranquilliser dart could have taken minutes to work, so its response team shot Harambe.
He was 17. He was born on 27 May 1999 and died the day after his birthday.
It is a half-joking, half-sincere tribute to Harambe and a reference to 2016 internet culture, often used when something feels like the world has gone off course.
